newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian president chooses new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Estonian president chooses new prime minister.

text.p: Estonia's president on Thursday named the Baltic state's new prime minister as Mart Siiman, a leading politician from one of the ruling parties.
Siiman, head of the parliament faction of the ruling Coalition Party, has 14 days to form a government and present it to parliament, the office of President Lennart Meri said.
"The Estonian president named today as candidate prime minister Mart Siiman and gave him the task of forming the republic's government," Meri's office said in a statement.
Siiman comes to power after former premier Tiit Vaehi, a veteran politician who had been in office since April 1995.
Vaehi stepped down after only narrowly winning a parliament no-confidence vote earlier this month amid allegations he took part in shady privatisation deals.
Estonia, which regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, is ruled by a minority administration of the Coalition Party and a bloc of rural parties.
Siiman, a television and radio manager from the pre-Soviet and post-Soviet era, believes he can muster the support of two thirds of the 101-seat parliament.
He is seen as a man who has operated in the political background with a low popular profile but is expected to be a compromise candidate that can unite squabbling political parties.
However, it is still not clear whether other parties will join the government although talks have been held.
Despite frequent political turmoil, Estonia has managed to carry on with the economic reforms which analysts say has made it one of the success stories of the former Soviet Union.
Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states with a population of just 1.5 million, has carried out a fast privatisation programme and been praised for having an open economy.
It also attracted much foreign investment, particularly from Finland, just 80 km (50 miles) to the north.
